explanation: The fork() system call in C creates a new process by duplicating the calling process, known as the child process. It is used to enable multitasking and process creation in Unix-like systems. The child inherits the parent's signal dispositions, including any signal handlers, because it receives a copy of the parent's memory image, ensuring consistency and allowing the child to respond to signals in the same way as the parent until modified.
